items.title: 6.9.3 Calculating the enthalpy change of solution

source_refs.note: Topic 6.9.3, printed pages 133-134 (Figure 6.7); Sample Problem 6.8. The print labels the final answer 'delta Hhyd [NaF]' where delta Hsol is meant.

blocks.text: The enthalpy change of solution, or of hydration, can be calculated by constructing an enthalpy cycle and using Hess's law. The gaseous ions form the ionic solid (lattice energy) and the ionic solid dissolves (enthalpy of solution); the gaseous ions also go directly to ions in aqueous solution (enthalpy of hydration of cation and anion). From the cycle, delta Hlatt + delta Hsol = delta Hhyd.

blocks.alt: Energy triangle of three light-blue boxes: 'gaseous ions' (top left), 'ionic solid' (top right) and 'ions in aqueous solution' (bottom). Arrow gaseous ions to ionic solid: lattice energy, delta H(o)latt. Arrow gaseous ions to ions in aqueous solution: enthalpy change of hydration of cation and anion, delta H(o)hyd. Arrow ionic solid to ions in aqueous solution: enthalpy change of solution, delta H(o)sol. A red dashed arrow runs round the indirect route.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.7: Energy cycle of formation of an aqueous solution of an ionic solid using Hess' law (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.7).

blocks.alt: Enthalpy cycle for sodium fluoride: Na+(g) + F-(g) to NaF(s), delta H(o)latt = -902 kJ mol-1; Na+(g) + F-(g) to Na+(aq) + F-(aq) (+aq), with delta H(o)hyd [Na+] = -406 kJ mol-1 and delta H(o)hyd [F-] = -506 kJ mol-1; NaF(s) to Na+(aq) + F-(aq), delta H(o)sol. A red dashed arrow marks the indirect route.
blocks.caption: Enthalpy cycle of sodium fluoride (Sample Problem 6.8, Step 1) (original drawing after the figure printed on p134 of the textbook).
